name: gitkit-vscode
description: Everyday git and GitHub, made visual and safe: status at a glance, branch lanes, conflict forecasts, undo, and a visual GitHub Actions builder.
author: Sam Selvaraj

untrustedWorkspaces.description: GitKit runs git, which can run programs a repository configures (hooks, fsmonitor), so it waits until you trust the folder.

virtualWorkspaces.description: GitKit runs git on the files on your disk, which a virtual workspace doesn't have.

gitkit.autoFetchMinutes.description: How often GitKit checks the remote for new commits while VS Code is focused, in minutes. 0 turns it off.

enumDescriptions: A pop-up when someone pushes to your branch or to main, and a count on the GitKit icon until you look.
Only the count on the GitKit icon.
gitkit.newCommitAlerts.description: How GitKit tells you about other people's new commits that it finds while checking the remote.

gitkit.repoScanDepth.description: How many folder levels below each workspace folder GitKit looks for git repositories.

gitkit.followActiveEditor.description: When the workspace has several repositories, switch to the one containing the file you're editing.

gitkit.mainBranchColor.description: Colour of the main branch (main/master) in the graph and Branch Map. One of blue, green, purple, orange, red, yellow, or any CSS colour such as #e5534b.

gitkit.commitGuard.enabled.description: Before committing, warn about likely secrets, .env and key files, and very large files.

gitkit.commitGuard.maxFileSizeMB.description: Files bigger than this (in MB) get a warning before they're committed.

enumDescriptions: Next to the repo, in <repo>.worktrees/: nothing inside your project changes.
Inside the repo, in .worktrees/ (kept out of git status through .git/info/exclude, not .gitignore).
gitkit.worktrees.location.description: Where GitKit creates new worktrees. Worktrees made elsewhere (by the CLI or other tools) are listed wherever they are.

gitkit.worktrees.setupCommand.markdownDescription: A command to run in a new worktree, in a terminal you can see, e.g. `npm install`. A fresh worktree has no installed dependencies, so agents often need this before their first command.

gitkit.worktrees.copyFiles.markdownDescription: Files or folders git ignores that a new worktree should get a copy of, relative to the repo, e.g. `[".vscode/settings.json"]`. Nothing is copied unless listed here: add `.env` only if you want your secrets duplicated into each worktree.

gitkit.checkpoints.onAgentStart.markdownDescription: Save a checkpoint of a worktree's files when a coding agent starts in a terminal there (see `#gitkit.checkpoints.agentCommands#`). Checkpoints never touch your files, staging area or stashes, and show up in the Undo list.

gitkit.checkpoints.agentCommands.description: Terminal commands that start a coding agent. Also matched through npx, pnpm dlx and similar.

gitkit.checkpoints.keep.description: How many checkpoints to keep per worktree. Older ones are dropped, so they don't keep files alive in the repo forever.

gitkit.checkpoints.maxAgeDays.description: Checkpoints older than this many days are dropped.

gitkit.identities.markdownDescription: Which email to commit with, by repo. Before committing, GitKit warns if the repo's email doesn't match the first rule that applies. Example: `[{ "remote": "github.com/my-university-org/**", "email": "me@university.edu" }, { "folder": "D:/Work", "email": "me@company.com" }]`

remote.description: Glob on the remote, like github.com/my-org/** (ssh and https URLs both work).

name.description: Optional name to set along with the email.

gitkit.ciStatus.description: Show GitHub check results for the latest pushed commit. Public repos need no sign-in.

scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build
